> The test waits until the status is set, so even a resource-constrained env should just wait a little longer ... the failures I see are bailing out of that loop after only one wait (105ms), so something is turning that field non-nil without populating the expected results

i'm not familiar with this area of the code. it does appear to be waiting for the TypeChecking struct to be populated, but not for the Warnings slice to be populated.

logically (without trying to find the code):
- if TypeChecking is expected to be populated with Warnings _during_ a Get call _after_ the Create call, we are catching a flake bug.
- if the Warnings in the TypeChecking are populated async of the TypeChecking then we are catching a test flake and the test must be updated to wait for the Warnings too.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8f80e0146726c42edefdfaeda6123872a5ec0981/test/e2e/apimachinery/validatingadmissionpolicy.go#L352-L365

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/policy/validating/typechecking.go#L108

the problem is not reproducible in the unit test here if the interval is set to a lower value <= 100ms and tested with the `stress` tool.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/validatingadmissionpolicystatus/controller_test.go#L118
but that's with a fake client.

this extra err check seems redundant:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/validatingadmissionpolicystatus/controller_test.go#L137-L139

it might be worth temporary adding a print of the crd and policy before this line:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/apimachinery/validatingadmissionpolicy.go#L365
then allow this test to flake again and inspect the results.

> /assign @jiahuif the type checking code owner

@jiahuif, the API field doc indicates a non-nil value means type checking is complete:

```
	// The results of type checking for each expression.
	// Presence of this field indicates the completion of the type checking.
	// +optional
	TypeChecking *TypeChecking `json:"typeChecking,omitempty" protobuf:"bytes,2,opt,name=typeChecking"`
```

It doesn't look like the type checker has any way to signal that it was lacking some information needed to complete type checking, and will record an empty set of warnings if it is:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b3926d137cd2964cd3a04088ded30845910547b1/pkg/controller/validatingadmissionpolicystatus/controller.go#L148-L160

are there any scenarios where a laggy REST mapper or informer can make the controller think it completed type checking but be missing some info that makes it produce an empty list of warnings?

I think our options are:
1. change the test to wait for non-empty warnings in the status (not just non-nil typeChecking)
2. change the controller to not write an empty typeChecking stanza if it fails to type check in some way

option 2 seems better for observers, but I don't know how invasive that is
@liggitt option 2 feels like we are creating a hole? (folks will see warnings sometimes and sometimes they don't?)
Option 2 might cause confusion especially when deleting existing warnings from typechecking field.(We will remove the typechecking warning if observed the fix in schema)

> Option 2 might cause confusion especially when deleting existing warnings from typechecking field.(We will remove the typechecking warning if observed the fix in schema)

I'm not suggesting deleting existing warnings, but it appears we are currently reporting an empty typeChecking stanza when we have not actually finished type checking... that doesn't match the API docs and is likely confusing to API clients (it's confusing our own e2e test we wrote based on the documented behavior)

Ignoring errors while finishing the type checking is intended behavior defined by the original KEP. Can we go back to change the tests to do a retry loop until the CRD appears in the RESTMapper? The root problem of laggy RESTMapper seems out of the scope of this test case.

> if #123870 is fixing the test then it's masking a state not guaranteed by the field comment:
> 
> > // Presence of this field indicates the completion of the type checking.
> 
> i guess @liggitt already explained that above.

The type checking is completed with this field set to non-nil. The problem is that the type checking finishes with error, and it cause some of the referred types to be ignored.

> 
> The type checking is completed with this field set to non-nil. The problem is that the type checking finishes with error, and it cause some of the referred types to be ignored.

should this error be surfaced to the user and does that need an e2e test?

> > The type checking is completed with this field set to non-nil. The problem is that the type checking finishes with error, and it cause some of the referred types to be ignored.
> 
> should this error be surfaced to the user and does that need an e2e test?

No. The KEP defines that errors will be ignored. However, there is a next step https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123350 to make the type checker reacts on CRD changes, which handles the case when the CRD schema is late for the type checking.
i think users might be confused by this behavior (the same way people on this thread are) even if it's documented in a KEP, so a field comment update feels worth it, at minimum.

The current type checking is informational and only works on ValidatingAdmissionPolicy. If the CRD is created after type checking or CRD created but not showing in schema watcher yet, the error would be ignored. And it will not retry as long as ValidatingAdmissionPolicy remains unchanged. There is a PR for adding retry with schema resolver raised in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123350 which will solve the issue entirely. In current case, the guess would be schema watcher is slow so it didn't have crd info yet when performing typechecking.

The temporary fix by @jiahuif in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123873 will resolve the test flaky by adding manually retry.

The field comment of `// Presence of this field indicates the completion of the type checking.` makes sense to me since it indicates the completion of the type checking but not handling the case where the CRD has not been created or created but not showing in schema watcher yet. FYI The [documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/validating-admission-policy/#type-checking) says `Type Checking does not apply to CRDs, including matched CRD types and reference of paramKind. The support for CRDs will come in future release.`

I agree it might not fit in conformance test. Not sure about the conformance test criteria.
cc
/triage accepted

review_comments: No this won't solve the problem. The type checker will not retry when the RESTMapper does not yet recognize the requested CRD. Here, TypeChecking would be empty but non-nil, and the wait will time out.
